Q: MongoDB: Indexing Design Fundamentals Skill Check - Question 4 A:

Justification is in the course: indexes should cover fields used in filters and sort, and sort fields must be just after the fields used for equality filter, so only { userId: 1, dueDate: -1, priority: 1 }. Chosing { userId: 1, dueDate: -1} is ok but covering all filters in query 2 is better regarding this.

Q: Frontend of backend first? A:

For testing you can always make your program work with CLI parameters, frontend can come later.
If you start at the frontend you can design how it feels to use first, before getting into the details of implementation.
Both ways can work, as long as you and your company you work at decide together which one makes sense for you.

And if you are the one deciding that, why worry? You can't be done earlier than you are.
If you're worried that somebody in your company might get mad at you, talk to people what they expect.

Q: Why is PostgreSQL TRUNCATE table MVCC unsafe A:

Because MVCC requires to keep the deleted rows for queries which started before to continue to read a consistent state. Truncate removes this versions history. Think of like a drop+recreate, and that's why it is fast.

Q: How to update a review that had old commits before it? A:

I think you have to put the id1 id3 at the end as rbt options won't be included correctly after that.

For example if you want to post changes between commits id1 & id3 to review 2 it would be:

rbt post -r id_review_2 id1:id3
